stops.name: Holuhraun
stops.detail: Holuhraun is a lava field in the Icelandic highlands north of Vatnajökull that was formed by fissure eruptions.

stops.name: Jökulsá á Fjöllum
stops.detail: This refers to the numerous headwaters (Icelandic kvísl = branch; branched stream) of the Jökulsá á Fjöllum located within and near it, which flow here from the Dyngjujökull glacier.

stops.name: Bárðarbunga
stops.detail: However, recent studies show that the composition of the lava suggests it belongs to the Bárðarbunga system.

stops.name: Askja
stops.detail: Until recently, the lava field was attributed to the Askja volcanic system.

stops.name: Hauptkrater mit einem Lavasee
stops.detail: As the eruption progressed, a main crater with a lava lake formed, which now fed the lava flows.
